title: LABMATE: Language Model Based Multi-Agent System to Accelerate Catalysis Experiments
problem: LLMs hallucinate and cannot reliably perform complex simulation tasks needed for materials science and catalysis research; researchers lack integrated tools for coordinating simulation, data analysis, and literature review.
motivation: Catalysis research requires coordinating multiple computational and experimental tasks (simulations, particle analysis, data analysis, literature review, hypothesis generation). A single unified framework can accelerate the research process while maintaining scientific rigor through human-in-the-loop validation.
method: Multi-agent system architecture where LLM agents are orchestrated to handle specific tasks (simulation submission, particle tracking, data analysis, literature review, hypothesis generation) with human experts maintaining validation control. Domain-specific prompting and tool integration.
key_novelty: Human-in-the-loop multi-agent framework that distributes LLM agents across domain-specific tasks rather than relying on a single LLM for all decisions; domain-agnostic architecture enabling cross-domain adoption.
contributions: LAB-MATE framework achieving chemistry/materials science benchmark performance on par with frontier LLMs
Modular agent-based architecture separating concerns (simulation, analysis, literature, hypothesis)
Human expert validation layer preventing hallucination-induced errors
Demonstrated acceleration of research workflows across simulation and analysis

metrics.benchmark_performance: Comparable to frontier LLMs on Chemistry and Materials Science segments

limitations: Requires human expert validation (not fully autonomous)
Limited to domains with well-defined agent tasks
Abstract-only analysis prevents detailed performance metrics assessment
primary_theme: AI-enhanced scientific computing via multi-agent orchestration
